Course Syllabus

Placement 360 – The Complete Tech Interview Program
AI Toolkit for Developers

Programming Language

Choose the programming language that best aligns with your goals and build a strong foundation in software development through structured learning and hands-on coding.

  • C++: Master programming fundamentals, object-oriented programming, STL, memory management, and efficient problem-solving techniques.
  • Java: Learn core Java, object-oriented programming, collections, exception handling, multithreading, and modern application development concepts.
  • Python: Build a strong programming foundation by mastering Python syntax, data structures, functions, object-oriented programming, and automation with clean, readable code.

Data Structures & Algorithms

Build a strong foundation in Data Structures and Algorithms by mastering core concepts, problem-solving techniques, and algorithm optimization.

Topics Covered

  • Analysis of Algorithms: Time & Space Complexity, Asymptotic Analysis (Big O, Big Theta, Big Omega)
  • Mathematics: Prime Numbers, GCD, LCM, Modular Arithmetic, Sieve of Eratosthenes
  • Bit Manipulation: Bitwise Operators, Bit Masking, XOR Tricks, Binary Operations
  • Recursion: Recursive Thinking, Tail Recursion, Tower of Hanoi, Josephus Problem
  • Arrays: Prefix Sum, Sliding Window, Two Pointers, Kadane's Algorithm
  • Strings: Pattern Matching, KMP, Rabin-Karp, String Hashing
  • Searching & Sorting: Binary Search, Merge Sort, Quick Sort, Heap Sort
  • Hashing: Hash Maps, Frequency Counting, Subarray & Pair Problems
  • Linked Lists: Singly, Doubly & Circular Lists, Reversal, Loop Detection
  • Stacks, Queues & Deques: Balanced Parentheses, Stock Span, Sliding Window, Queue Applications

Advanced Data Structures & Algorithms

Master advanced data structures and algorithmic techniques used to solve complex computational problems efficiently.

Topics Covered

  • Trees & BST: Tree Traversals, LCA, Serialization, BST Operations, Balanced Trees
  • Heaps: Min/Max Heap, Priority Queue, Heap Sort, Top-K Problems
  • Graphs: BFS, DFS, Shortest Paths, MST, Topological Sort, Union-Find
  • Greedy Algorithms: Activity Selection, Fractional Knapsack, Job Scheduling
  • Backtracking: N-Queens, Sudoku Solver, Rat in a Maze, Permutations
  • Dynamic Programming: Memoization, Tabulation, LCS, LIS, Coin Change, DP on Trees
  • Trie: Prefix Search, Auto-complete, Word Dictionary, String Queries
  • Segment Trees & Binary Indexed Trees: Range Queries, Lazy Propagation, Fenwick Tree
  • Disjoint Set Union (DSU): Union-Find, Path Compression, Cycle Detection, Kruskal's Algorithm

Object-Oriented Programming & Low-Level Design

Master the fundamentals of software design by learning object-oriented principles, design patterns, and low-level system design used in modern software development.

Topics Covered

  • Object-Oriented Design (OOD): OOAD concepts, UML Diagrams, Use Case, Class, Sequence, and Activity Diagrams.
  • SOLID Principles: Build clean, scalable, maintainable, and loosely coupled software using the five SOLID design principles.
  • Design Patterns: Learn Creational, Structural, and Behavioral Design Patterns including Factory, Singleton, Builder, Adapter, Facade, Observer, Strategy, and more.
  • Low-Level Design (LLD): Design real-world systems like Movie Ticket Booking, Car Parking Lot, and Elevator System using industry-standard design practices.

Develop practical problem-solving skills required for software engineering interviews.

1: The AI Toolkit & Developer Setup

  • Map of AI tools: LLMs, code assistants, AI search, agents
  • Tool categories: chat models, IDE copilots, CLI agents
  • Evaluation framework: accuracy, context window, cost, latency
  • When AI helps vs. when it hurts: real limitations
  • Setting up an AI-powered dev environment in 30 minutes
  • Live experiment: solving the same problem with multiple tools

2: Prompt Engineering & Vibe Coding

  • Vibe coding: natural language to code (fast prototyping)
  • Anatomy of a developer prompt: role, context, task, constraints
  • Zero-shot to few-shot escalation strategy
  • Chain-of-thought prompting for better reasoning
  • Iterative prompting and fixing hallucinations

3: Spec-Driven Development with AI

  • Transition from prompts to structured specifications
  • Writing clear technical specs before code generation
  • Few-shot prompting with real codebase patterns
  • Generating reliable code aligned with requirements
  • Reducing ambiguity and improving determinism

4: RAG Systems & Context-Aware AI

  • Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) fundamentals
  • Embeddings, vector databases, semantic search
  • Connecting AI to codebases, docs, and internal data
  • Building developer assistants using RAG
  • Limitations and failure modes of RAG systems
